skill.name: azure-storage-blob-ts
skill.description: TypeScript and JavaScript reference for Azure Blob Storage operations with @azure/storage-blob. Covers authentication, containers, blobs, streaming, SAS tokens, metadata, and platform differences.
skill.summary: Use Azure Blob Storage SDK examples for TypeScript apps and automation.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by markdown fences, TypeScript template literals, Azure endpoint examples, and credential configuration snippets. No prompt injection, hidden execution path, or exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md. One medium semantic concern remains: SAS examples show broad permissions that users should narrow before production use.

remediation.issue: SAS examples show broad container and account permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Replace broad permission strings with least-privilege examples and explain when each permission is required.

remediation.issue: Credential examples rely on sensitive environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning to avoid logging keys, connection strings, or SAS tokens.

remediation.issue: Examples are educational and may be copied directly.
remediation.suggestion: Label placeholder paths, account names, and permission sets as examples that require production review.

semantic_findings.title: Overly Broad SAS Permission Examples
semantic_findings.description: The SAS examples include container permissions for read, add, create, write, delete, and list, and an account SAS example with all listed permissions. Users could copy these broad permissions into production.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The permission strings are visible in the SAS generation examples and exceed least privilege for many workflows. The file also recommends short-lived tokens, so the issue is risky guidance rather than malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Azure Blob Storage work requires correct SDK patterns and careful credential handling. This skill gives focused TypeScript examples for clients, containers, blobs, streaming, and SAS access.
actual_capabilities: Shows installation and authentication patterns for Azure Blob Storage clients.
Provides container create, list, and delete examples.
Covers blob upload, download, list, delete, and copy operations.
Demonstrates file, stream, buffer, browser, and metadata workflows.
Explains blob SAS, container SAS, account SAS, and platform differences.
Includes Azure SDK error handling and TypeScript type references.
limitations: It is reference documentation, not an executable integration or tested helper library.
Examples use placeholders and require real Azure account, container, and credential values.
Some examples only work in Node.js, while browser support differs.
It does not cover private endpoints, lifecycle policies, or infrastructure deployment.

use_cases.title: Add Blob Storage to a TypeScript Service
use_cases.description: Use the client hierarchy and upload examples to add storage operations to a backend service.

use_cases.title: Prepare Browser Upload Access
use_cases.description: Design short-lived SAS flows for browser uploads without placing storage keys in client code.

use_cases.title: Review Azure Storage SDK Usage
use_cases.description: Compare existing code against documented SDK patterns for authentication, streaming, metadata, and errors.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Blob Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new TypeScript project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create an Azure Blob Storage client in TypeScript using DefaultAzureCredential and an account name from the environment.

prompt_templates.title: Upload and Download Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to upload a local file to a container and download a blob to a local path using @azure/storage-blob.

prompt_templates.title: Design Browser Upload SAS
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a browser upload flow that uses a server-generated SAS token with the minimum required permissions and a short expiration.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Storage Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Blob Storage integration for credential exposure, broad SAS permissions, missing error handling, and inefficient streaming.

output_examples.input: I need a secure browser upload flow for customer files.
output: Recommend generating short-lived SAS tokens on the server.
Limit permissions to the exact upload operation and target container.
Keep account keys and connection strings out of browser code.

output_examples.input: I need to upload large files from a Node.js worker.
output: Use stream-based uploads for large files.
Tune buffer size and concurrency for memory and throughput.
Add progress handling and Azure RestError handling.

output_examples.input: I need to choose the right authentication method.
output: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential for managed Azure workloads.
Use connection strings only when identity-based access is unavailable.
Use short-lived SAS tokens for delegated client access.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential and managed identity before shared keys or connection strings.
Generate SAS tokens with the shortest practical lifetime and minimum required permissions.
Use streaming APIs for large files and handle Azure RestError status codes explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not place account keys, connection strings, or broad SAS tokens in browser code.
Do not copy all-permission SAS examples into production without reducing scope.
Do not load large blobs fully into memory when stream-based APIs are available.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides SDK reference examples that a developer can adapt in their own code.

faq.question: Which Azure package does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers @azure/storage-blob for TypeScript and JavaScript projects.

faq.question: Can it help with authentication choices?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares DefaultAzureCredential, connection strings, shared keys, and SAS token access.

faq.question: Does it support browser examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes browser upload patterns and notes which SDK features are Node.js only.

faq.question: Does it include SAS token generation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes blob, container, and account SAS examples with permission and expiration settings.

faq.question: Should I use the examples unchanged in production?
faq.answer: No. Review permissions, credential storage, error handling, and environment-specific security controls first.
